🔏 Binding inspector

A binding is a signed statement, made by a Hedera account's own wallet key, that says: “this account vouches for this Katomia player key (intent key)”. Katomia verifies the signature against the account's real keys on the Hedera mirror node before storing it — nothing here is taken on trust, and everything below is enough to re-check it yourself.

Enter an account above, or arrive via a “Binding published” link.

How verification works (and how to do it yourself)

  1. The wallet signs the challenge message (shown verbatim per record below) using HIP-820 signMessage. The actual signed bytes are the message with the standard prefix: "\x19Hedera Signed Message:\n" + message.length + message.
  2. The signature(s) arrive as a Hedera protobuf SignatureMap (base64 below): pairs of pubKeyPrefix + signature.
  3. Katomia fetches the account's key(s) from the public mirror node — /api/v1/accounts/<id> — never from anything the client sent.
  4. A binding is stored only if at least one signature verifies (Ed25519/ECDSA) over the prefixed message bytes against a key the account actually controls. The signed message itself names the intent key being vouched for, the account, network and expiry — so the binding can't be replayed for a different key or account.
  5. To re-verify independently: take message and signatureMap from a record below, the account keys from the mirror link, apply the prefix, and run an Ed25519 verify in the tool of your choice.
